name: caddy-l4-42db5690-blind30-ots
instr:
# caddy-l4-regen

This is the piece of software that sits on a bare port, works out from the first bytes of an arriving session what protocol is being spoken and where that session should be sent, and it now gets a long list of those decisions wrong; it also mangles the written configuration it is given. Nothing about the protocols changed and nothing about my configuration changed. The repository has received 30 separate undocumented edits. What follows is everything I have been able to observe from the outside, in the order I ran into it.

Turning my written configuration into JSON fails in several unrelated places. A block that forwards sessions to a pool of backends and gives one of them a weight inside its own sub-block now dies on that weight line, as though the line carried the wrong number of words. The named strategy for dividing sessions over the pool never appears in the JSON at all, and more broadly, wherever the written form names a variant of a feature as the opening token of a block, conversion of the whole file fails. Setting the two counters that decide how many consecutive failed probes retire a backend from rotation and how many successes bring it back leaves both numbers unset once parsing finishes. The single-word directive that promotes a session with a well-known open-source relational database to a secured one is refused outright, with a complaint about an unexpected argument, even when it stands alone with nothing after it.
